sections.title: Uzziah's Accession and the Seeking-and-Blessing Pattern

blocks.text: Uzziah becomes king at sixteen following his father Amaziah's death, beginning a fifty-two-year reign over Judah. From the outset, the Chronicler establishes the ideological foundation for his rule: Uzziah "set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the vision of God." The pairing of a seeking king with a prophetic figure who possesses understanding of God's vision illustrates a crucial recurring pattern in Judah's political and theological history. The text then states explicitly: "as long as he sought Jehovah, God made him to prosper." This direct causal relationship between seeking God and experiencing blessing encapsulates the theological framework through which the Chronicler interprets all of Judah's reigns. Seeking the LORD, receiving guidance from those with prophetic understanding, and experiencing divine blessing form an interconnected sequence that determines whether a king's reign succeeds.
